classification.difficultyReason: Finds each vertex from the zero of the linear argument and uses intercepts, reflection and vertical scaling to sketch four familiar absolute-value graphs.

answer.worked: $x-1=0$ gives the vertex $(1,0)$. At $x=0$, $y=|-1|=1$. Draw an upward V through $(0,1)$ with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V with arrowheads, x- and y-axes, ticks at the vertex abscissa 1 and y-intercept 1, and curve equation. No grid.

answer.worked: $2x+3=0$ gives $x=-\frac32$, so the vertex is $(-\frac32,0)$. At $x=0$, $y=3$. Draw an upward V through $(0,3)$ with slopes $-2$ and $2$.

spec.description: Upward V with arrowheads and labelled intercept ticks; no grid.

answer.worked: $2-x=0$ gives the vertex $(2,0)$. At $x=0$, $y=-|2|=-2$. The negative sign reflects the absolute value graph in the $x$-axis, giving a downward V.

spec.description: Downward V with arrowheads; vertex tick 2 above the x-axis and y-intercept tick -2 to the left; no grid.

answer.worked: $6-3x=0$ gives the vertex $(2,0)$. At $x=0$, $y=-|6|=-6$. Since $y=-3|x-2|$, draw a downward V with slopes $3$ and $-3$.

spec.description: Downward V with arrowheads; vertex tick 2 and corrected y-intercept tick -6. Original teacher label is 6 below the x-axis. No grid.
